_comment: Guided tour for the standalone metadata editor. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to press them; targets are the names the window and the editor widget remember.

steps.title: What this edits
steps.text: A metadata record as a JSON file: typed fields from a schema plus free-form key/value entries. The same editor sits inside Burst Selection (the flrCIF metadata of an export) and the Zenodo deposit (a record's metadata); here it edits a file on its own.

steps.title: Pick the schema
steps.text: free-form has no typed fields, flrCIF the experiment keys of a burst export (pH, temperature, ionic strength, labelling fractions), Zenodo a deposit's fields. Switching keeps what has been typed.

await.hint: Pick a schema from the list.

steps.title: Open a file
steps.text: Open a .json object. Keys of the schema fill its fields; every other key becomes a free-form entry, nothing is dropped.

await.hint: Press Open… and pick a metadata file.

steps.title: Add an entry beyond the schema
steps.text: Type a key and a value, then Add entry. An existing key is replaced; a schema key edits that field. Select a row in the table below and press Delete to remove it.

await.hint: Type a key and a value, then press Add entry.

steps.title: Apply writes the file
steps.text: Every problem is listed in red above the buttons (a number that is not a number, a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD, a required field left empty); Apply stays grey until the list is empty. Apply writes the open file and the editor stays on it; Cancel reverts to what is on disk.

await.hint: Fix what is listed, then press Apply.

steps.title: Or write a new file
steps.text: Save as… writes the entries to a new file and makes it the open one.
